items.title: 클래스별 책임
items.question: 클래스별 책임
paragraphs: CameraManager는 장치를 열거하고 파이프라인 관리자와 연결하며, 애플리케이션에 카메라 접근을 제공하고 카메라 객체를 소유하면서 핫플러그와 핫언플러그에 따른 수명을 관리하는 libcamera의 진입점입니다. CameraManager 인스턴스는 한 번에 하나만 존재할 수 있으며, 기존 인스턴스를 삭제하기 전에 추가 인스턴스를 만들면 동작이 정의되지 않습니다.

Camera는 단일 이미지 소스에서 하나 이상의 이미지 스트림을 생성할 수 있는 카메라를 모델링하며, 장치의 설정과 제어 및 이미지 스트림 캡처를 위한 주요 인터페이스입니다. libcamera는 std::shared_ptr로 카메라 인스턴스의 수명을 관리하며, 인스턴스는 공유 포인터를 반환하는 create()로 생성해야 합니다. Camera의 생성자와 소멸자는 수동 생성과 파괴를 막기 위해 비공개입니다. Request는 애플리케이션이 프레임마다 버퍼와 컨트롤을 연결하고 카메라 장치의 처리를 위해 큐에 넣을 수 있게 하는 객체입니다.
Request 생성자에 전달한 cookie는 요청에 저장되는 애플리케이션용 불투명 값이며, 언제든지 cookie()로 읽을 수 있습니다.

items.reason: 로컬 그림은 세 클래스의 책임과 Camera의 공유 수명, 생성 및 참조 관계를 직접 보여 줍니다. 인용된 발췌와 Camera::createRequest 구현이 표시된 관계를 뒷받침합니다.

items.title: 상태와 허용 호출
items.question: 상태와 허용 호출
paragraphs: 카메라가 Available 상태에서 acquire()에 성공하면 Acquired 상태가 됩니다.

Camera::configure()는 CameraAcquired부터 CameraConfigured까지의 접근을 검사해 결과가 음수이면 그 값을 반환하고, 각 설정의 스트림을 nullptr로 설정한 뒤 validate()가 CameraConfiguration::Valid가 아니면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. 이후 PipelineHandler::configure의 반환값이 0이 아니면 그 값을 반환하고, 성공하면 활성 스트림을 비운 뒤 각 설정의 cfg.stream()을 확인합니다. 스트림이 null이면 LOG로 Fatal 메시지를 출력하고 그 뒤 활성 스트림을 비우고 -EINVAL을 반환하는 구문이 있지만, Fatal 로그는 메시지 출력 직후 프로그램을 종료하며, 모든 스트림 처리를 마치면 상태를 Configured로 설정하고 0을 반환합니다.

Configured 상태에서 start()가 성공하면 카메라는 Running 상태가 됩니다. 카메라는 Running 상태에서 stop()을 호출하면 Stopping 상태로 진입합니다. 카메라는 Stopping 상태에서 정지 처리가 끝나면 Configured 상태로 돌아갑니다. release()는 Available 상태에서는 상태를 유지하고, Acquired 또는 Configured 상태에서는 Available로 바꿉니다.

호출자는 카메라가 Configured 또는 Running 상태일 때만 Camera::createRequest()를 호출할 수 있습니다. 호출자는 카메라가 Running 상태일 때만 Camera::queueRequest를 호출할 수 있습니다. 카메라가 실행 중이 아니어서 요청을 큐에 넣을 수 없으면 -EACCES를 반환합니다. Camera::start()는 카메라가 Configured 상태일 때만 호출할 수 있습니다.
Camera 클래스는 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 함수들을 일반적으로 서로 동기화하지 않습니다. 호출자는 필요한 경우 이 함수들이 동기화되도록 해야 합니다.

paragraphs: Camera::queueRequest()는 캡처 요청을 큐에 넣는 데 성공하면 0을 반환하고, 실패하면 음수 오류 코드를 반환합니다. 카메라가 시스템에서 분리되면 -ENODEV, 카메라가 실행 중이 아니면 -EACCES, 요청을 처리할 버퍼 메모리가 없으면 -ENOMEM을 반환합니다. 실행 상태를 확인하는 isAccessAllowed(Private::CameraRunning)의 결과가 음수이면 그 값을 그대로 반환합니다.
Camera::queueRequest()는 요청이 이 카메라에서 생성되지 않았으면 -EXDEV를 반환합니다. 요청의 상태가 Request::RequestPending이 아니거나 request->controls().infoMap()이 &controls()와 다르면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다.

애플리케이션은 createRequest()로 요청을 할당한 뒤 큐에 넣기 전에 캡처 버퍼를 적어도 하나 채워야 합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 카메라 상태·소유 카메라·요청 상태·제어 정보 검사 뒤에 버퍼 존재와 활성 스트림을 검사하며, 버퍼가 없거나 버퍼의 스트림이 활성 상태가 아니면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. 큐에 넣은 요청의 완료는 requestCompleted 신호로 알립니다.

Camera::stop()은 카메라가 실행 중이 아니면 실제 구현에서 0을 반환합니다. 실행 중이면 isAccessAllowed(Private::CameraRunning)을 검사하고 결과가 음수일 때 그 값을 그대로 반환합니다. 검사를 통과하면 상태를 CameraStopping으로 바꾸고 ConnectionTypeBlocking으로 PipelineHandler::stop을 호출한 뒤, 대기 중인 요청이 없다는 단언을 거쳐 상태를 CameraConfigured로 바꾸고 0을 반환합니다.
Camera::stop()의 API 계약은 캡처와 요청 처리를 즉시 중지하고, 대기 중인 모든 요청을 취소하여 오류 상태로 동기적으로 완료한다고 설명합니다. 반환값은 성공 시 0, 그 밖에는 음수 오류 코드이며, 카메라가 시스템에서 분리된 경우 -ENODEV를 명시합니다.

items.body:
Camera::queueRequest()는 캡처 요청을 큐에 넣는 데 성공하면 0을 반환하고, 실패하면 음수 오류 코드를 반환합니다. 카메라가 시스템에서 분리되면 -ENODEV, 카메라가 실행 중이 아니면 -EACCES, 요청을 처리할 버퍼 메모리가 없으면 -ENOMEM을 반환합니다. 실행 상태를 확인하는 isAccessAllowed(Private::CameraRunning)의 결과가 음수이면 그 값을 그대로 반환합니다.

Camera::queueRequest()는 요청이 이 카메라에서 생성되지 않았으면 -EXDEV를 반환합니다. 요청의 상태가 Request::RequestPending이 아니거나 request->controls().infoMap()이 &controls()와 다르면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다.

애플리케이션은 createRequest()로 요청을 할당한 뒤 큐에 넣기 전에 캡처 버퍼를 적어도 하나 채워야 합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 카메라 상태·소유 카메라·요청 상태·제어 정보 검사 뒤에 버퍼 존재와 활성 스트림을 검사하며, 버퍼가 없거나 버퍼의 스트림이 활성 상태가 아니면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. 큐에 넣은 요청의 완료는 requestCompleted 신호로 알립니다.

Camera::stop()은 카메라가 실행 중이 아니면 실제 구현에서 0을 반환합니다. 실행 중이면 isAccessAllowed(Private::CameraRunning)을 검사하고 결과가 음수일 때 그 값을 그대로 반환합니다. 검사를 통과하면 상태를 CameraStopping으로 바꾸고 ConnectionTypeBlocking으로 PipelineHandler::stop을 호출한 뒤, 대기 중인 요청이 없다는 단언을 거쳐 상태를 CameraConfigured로 바꾸고 0을 반환합니다.

Camera::stop()의 API 계약은 캡처와 요청 처리를 즉시 중지하고, 대기 중인 모든 요청을 취소하여 오류 상태로 동기적으로 완료한다고 설명합니다. 반환값은 성공 시 0, 그 밖에는 음수 오류 코드이며, 카메라가 시스템에서 분리된 경우 -ENODEV를 명시합니다.

LLM 그림 초안 · 사람 검토 전 작성 모델: cli/codex/gpt-6.1-terra 요소·전이 소스 근거 Camera::stop()은 모든 카메라 상태에서 호출할 수 있습니다. 호출자는 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 다른 함수와 호출을 동기화해야 합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 카메라가 실행 중인지 확인합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 실행 중이 아니면 상태를 바꾸지 않고 0을 반환합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 Private::CameraRunning에 대한 접근을 검사하고 결과가 음수인지 확인합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 접근 검사 결과가 음수이면 그 오류 코드를 반환합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 상태를 Private::CameraStopping으로 바꿉니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 PipelineHandler::stop을 동기 호출합니다. 대기 중인 모든 요청은 취소되고 오류 상태로 동기 완료됩니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 대기 중인 요청이 없는지 ASSERT로 확인합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 상태를 Private::CameraConfigured로 바꿉니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 중지를 마치고 0을 반환합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 실행 여부를 확인합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 실행 중이 아니면 바로 반환합니다. · !d->isRunning() [true] src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 실행 중이면 접근을 검사합니다. · !d->isRunning() [false] src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 검사 결과가 음수이면 반환합니다. · ret < 0 [true] src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 검사 결과가 음수가 아니면 상태를 바꿉니다. · ret < 0 [false] src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 상태를 바꾼 뒤 동기 중지를 호출합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 동기 중지가 끝나면 대기 요청을 확인합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 요청을 확인한 뒤 상태를 바꿉니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 상태를 바꾼 뒤 반환합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431

items.question: 어떤 API 호출에 threadsafe·상태 조건과 호출자 동기화 의무가 있고, 어떤 완료 함수를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니까?
paragraphs: Camera::createRequest()는 스레드 안전 함수입니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 스레드 안전 함수입니다. 호출자는 Camera::start와 Camera::stop을 각각 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 다른 함수들과 동기화해야 합니다.

파이프라인 핸들러는 completeBuffer()와 completeRequest()를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다. cancelRequest()에는 completeRequest()와 같은 규칙이 적용되므로 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다. Camera::requestComplete()는 요청 완료를 알리는 경로에서 requestCompleted.emit(request)를 호출해 requestCompleted 신호를 발행합니다.

그림 근거와 확인 범위 어떤 API 호출에 threadsafe·상태 조건과 호출자 동기화 의무가 있고, 어떤 완료 함수를 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니까? 앱 콜백 전달 방식은 이 그림 범위 밖입니다. 소스에 연결한 설계 해석입니다. 자동 연결 검사는 의미 승인이나 기기 실행 검증이 아닙니다. LLM 그림 초안 · 사람 검토 전 작성 모델: cli/codex/gpt-6.1-terra 요소·전이 소스 근거 createRequest()는 threadsafe이며 Configured 또는 Running 상태에서만 호출할 수 있습니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1243 Camera::queueRequest()는 threadsafe이며 Running 상태에서만 호출할 수 있습니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1308 Camera::start()는 Configured 상태에서만 호출할 수 있습니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1383 Camera::stop()은 어느 상태에서나 호출할 수 있으며, 카메라가 실행 중이 아니면 아무 작업도 하지 않습니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 caller는 시작과 중지를 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 다른 함수와 동기화해야 합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1383 · src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 마지막 버퍼가 완료되어도 요청은 자동 완료되지 않으며, 핸들러가 completeRequest()로 명시적으로 완료해야 합니다. src/libcamera/pipeline_handler.cpp:547 completeRequest()에는 완료된 요청을 순서 제약 없이 전달할 수 있지만, 요청은 애플리케이션에 제출 순서로 반환됩니다. src/libcamera/pipeline_handler.cpp:547 CameraManager 스레드는 파이프라인 완료 함수의 호출 문맥입니다. src/libcamera/pipeline_handler.cpp:547 PipelineHandler::cancelRequest()는 요청을 취소하고 완료하며, completeRequest()와 같은 규칙을 따릅니다. src/libcamera/pipeline_handler.cpp:547 애플리케이션은 생성한 요청에 캡처 버퍼를 하나 이상 채운 뒤 큐에 넣어야 합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1308 caller는 Camera::start()를 다른 상태 영향 함수와 동기화해야 합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1383 caller는 Camera::stop()을 다른 상태 영향 함수와 동기화해야 합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 핸들러는 요청을 completeRequest()로 명시적으로 완료해야 합니다. src/libcamera/pipeline_handler.cpp:547 PipelineHandler::completeBuffer()는 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다. src/libcamera/pipeline_handler.cpp:547 completeRequest()는 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다. src/libcamera/pipeline_handler.cpp:547 PipelineHandler::cancelRequest()에는 completeRequest()와 같은 규칙이 적용됩니다. src/libcamera/pipeline_handler.cpp:547

LLM 그림 초안 · 사람 검토 전 작성 모델: cli/codex/gpt-6.1-terra 요소·전이 소스 근거 createRequest()는 threadsafe이며 Configured 또는 Running 상태에서만 호출할 수 있습니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1243 Camera::queueRequest()는 threadsafe이며 Running 상태에서만 호출할 수 있습니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1308 Camera::start()는 Configured 상태에서만 호출할 수 있습니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1383 Camera::stop()은 어느 상태에서나 호출할 수 있으며, 카메라가 실행 중이 아니면 아무 작업도 하지 않습니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 caller는 시작과 중지를 카메라 상태에 영향을 주는 다른 함수와 동기화해야 합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1383 · src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 마지막 버퍼가 완료되어도 요청은 자동 완료되지 않으며, 핸들러가 completeRequest()로 명시적으로 완료해야 합니다. src/libcamera/pipeline_handler.cpp:547 completeRequest()에는 완료된 요청을 순서 제약 없이 전달할 수 있지만, 요청은 애플리케이션에 제출 순서로 반환됩니다. src/libcamera/pipeline_handler.cpp:547 CameraManager 스레드는 파이프라인 완료 함수의 호출 문맥입니다. src/libcamera/pipeline_handler.cpp:547 PipelineHandler::cancelRequest()는 요청을 취소하고 완료하며, completeRequest()와 같은 규칙을 따릅니다. src/libcamera/pipeline_handler.cpp:547 애플리케이션은 생성한 요청에 캡처 버퍼를 하나 이상 채운 뒤 큐에 넣어야 합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1308 caller는 Camera::start()를 다른 상태 영향 함수와 동기화해야 합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1383 caller는 Camera::stop()을 다른 상태 영향 함수와 동기화해야 합니다. src/libcamera/camera.cpp:1431 핸들러는 요청을 completeRequest()로 명시적으로 완료해야 합니다. src/libcamera/pipeline_handler.cpp:547 PipelineHandler::completeBuffer()는 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다. src/libcamera/pipeline_handler.cpp:547 completeRequest()는 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다. src/libcamera/pipeline_handler.cpp:547 PipelineHandler::cancelRequest()에는 completeRequest()와 같은 규칙이 적용됩니다. src/libcamera/pipeline_handler.cpp:547

items.title: 연결 해제와 대기 요청
items.question: 연결 해제 시 상태와 접근 결과는 어떻게 달라지고, 알림과 대기 요청 처리는 어떻게 이루어집니까?
paragraphs: Camera::Private::disconnect()는 현재 상태가 CameraRunning일 때만 CameraConfigured를 저장하며, 다른 상태에서는 이 저장을 생략합니다. 이후 상태와 관계없이 disconnected_를 true로 설정합니다. 주석에 따르면 상태 변경의 목적은 하드웨어가 제거될 때 카메라가 실행 중이었다면 애플리케이션이 카메라를 삭제하기 전에 자원을 해제하고 release()를 호출할 수 있도록 하는 것입니다.

Camera::Private::isAccessAllowed의 두 오버로드는 !allowDisconnected와 disconnected_가 모두 참이면 상태 검사 전에 -ENODEV를 반환합니다. 단일 상태 오버로드는 현재 상태가 state와 같으면, 범위 오버로드는 현재 상태가 low 이상 high 이하이면 0을 반환합니다. 상태가 맞지 않으면 먼저 state 또는 low와 high가 상태 이름 배열의 유효 범위에 있는지 ASSERT로 검사하며, 이 검사를 통과한 경로에서 오류 로그를 기록하고 -EACCES를 반환합니다. 오류 로그는 from 뒤에 ()를 붙여 출력하며, 상태 이름은 currentState와 state 또는 low와 high를 사용해 가져옵니다.
Camera::disconnect()는 _d()->disconnect()를 호출한 뒤 disconnected.emit()을 호출합니다.
실행 확인 항목: Camera::disconnect()의 TODO는 카메라가 실행 중 연결 해제될 때 대기 중인 요청을 처리하는 일을 남겨 둡니다. 발췌된 본문은 _d()->disconnect()를 호출한 다음 disconnected.emit()을 호출하며, 개별 요청을 취소하거나 완료하는 코드는 포함하지 않습니다.

items.body:
Camera::Private::disconnect()는 현재 상태가 CameraRunning일 때만 CameraConfigured를 저장하며, 다른 상태에서는 이 저장을 생략합니다. 이후 상태와 관계없이 disconnected_를 true로 설정합니다. 주석에 따르면 상태 변경의 목적은 하드웨어가 제거될 때 카메라가 실행 중이었다면 애플리케이션이 카메라를 삭제하기 전에 자원을 해제하고 release()를 호출할 수 있도록 하는 것입니다.

Camera::Private::isAccessAllowed의 두 오버로드는 !allowDisconnected와 disconnected_가 모두 참이면 상태 검사 전에 -ENODEV를 반환합니다. 단일 상태 오버로드는 현재 상태가 state와 같으면, 범위 오버로드는 현재 상태가 low 이상 high 이하이면 0을 반환합니다. 상태가 맞지 않으면 먼저 state 또는 low와 high가 상태 이름 배열의 유효 범위에 있는지 ASSERT로 검사하며, 이 검사를 통과한 경로에서 오류 로그를 기록하고 -EACCES를 반환합니다. 오류 로그는 from 뒤에 ()를 붙여 출력하며, 상태 이름은 currentState와 state 또는 low와 high를 사용해 가져옵니다.

Camera::disconnect()는 _d()->disconnect()를 호출한 뒤 disconnected.emit()을 호출합니다.

실행 확인 항목: Camera::disconnect()의 TODO는 카메라가 실행 중 연결 해제될 때 대기 중인 요청을 처리하는 일을 남겨 둡니다. 발췌된 본문은 _d()->disconnect()를 호출한 다음 disconnected.emit()을 호출하며, 개별 요청을 취소하거나 완료하는 코드는 포함하지 않습니다.
items.reason: 연결 해제 그림은 실행 상태에 따른 분기, 플래그 설정과 신호 발생 순서, 대기 요청 처리의 TODO 범위를 직접 보여 줍니다. 접근 결과 그림과 근거 표는 두 오버로드의 반환 분기를 보완합니다. 두 그림의 표시 내용은 해당 발췌와 부합합니다.

items.title: 요청 생성과 완료
items.question: 요청 생성과 완료
paragraphs: createRequest는 새로 만든 빈 Request 객체를 std::unique_ptr<Request>로 반환하며, 오류가 나면 nullptr을 반환합니다. 반환된 객체의 소유권은 호출자에게 넘어가며, 호출자가 이를 삭제할 책임을 가집니다. 요청은 완료 핸들러에서 삭제되거나, Request::reuse()로 상태를 초기화한 뒤 재사용될 수 있습니다. 호출자는 Request::addBuffer로 한 요청에 같은 스트림의 버퍼를 둘 이상 연결해서는 안 되며, 한 요청은 스트림당 버퍼를 하나만 포함할 수 있습니다.

Request::addBuffer()는 먼저 !stream 조건을 확인하고, 참이면 "Invalid stream reference" 오류 로그를 남긴 뒤 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. 다음으로 buffer->_d()->fence()가 남아 있으면 -EEXIST를 반환하므로, fence가 남아 있는 버퍼는 이 단계에서 등록되지 않습니다. 마지막으로 bufferMap_.try_emplace(stream, buffer)의 inserted가 false이면, 로그 "FrameBuffer already set for stream"과 함께 -EEXIST를 반환합니다.

!stream 검사, fence 검사, inserted 검사를 모두 통과하고 bufferMap_.try_emplace가 inserted가 true인 경우에만 buffer->_d()->setRequest(this)와 _d()->pending_.insert(buffer)가 이 순서대로 실행됩니다. 이 두 줄 뒤에는 fence 설정 분기가 이어지고, 함수는 return 0;으로 끝납니다. 애플리케이션은 createRequest()로 요청을 만든 뒤 queueRequest를 호출하기 전에 그 요청에 캡처 버퍼를 하나 이상 채워야 하며, 버퍼가 없는 요청은 큐에 넣지 않고 거부됩니다. Camera::queueRequest는 접근 검사에서 반환하지 않고 생성 카메라 검사에 도달한 경우, 요청을 생성한 카메라가 현재 카메라와 다르면 -EXDEV를 반환합니다.

Camera::queueRequest는 접근 검사와 요청을 생성한 카메라 검사를 통과해 상태 검사에 도달한 경우, request->status()가 Request::RequestPending과 일치하지 않으면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 접근, 요청을 생성한 카메라, 요청 상태 검사에서 반환하지 않고 controls 검사에 도달한 경우, request->controls().infoMap()이 Camera::controls()의 주소와 다르면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다.

Camera::queueRequest가 앞선 접근·요청 생성 카메라·요청 상태·controls 검사를 통과해 이 검사에 도달하면, buffers 목록이 비어 있는 경우 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. 앞선 검사에서는 접근 검사 결과가 음수이면 그 값을 반환하고, 요청을 만든 카메라가 다르면 -EXDEV를, 요청 상태나 controls 검사가 실패하면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. Camera::queueRequest가 앞선 검사와 빈 버퍼 검사를 통과해 스트림 순회에 도달한 경우, 요청의 각 스트림이 activeStreams_에 포함되어 있는지 검사하고 포함되지 않은 스트림이 있으면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다.

Camera::queueRequest()는 요청 검사를 마친 뒤 ConnectionTypeQueued를 지정해 invokeMethod로 PipelineHandler::queueRequest를 호출하고, 그 호출 뒤에 0을 반환합니다. 이 0은 invokeMethod 호출 뒤의 반환값이며, 요청 완료는 카메라가 requestCompleted 신호로 별도로 알립니다.

items.body:
createRequest는 새로 만든 빈 Request 객체를 std::unique_ptr<Request>로 반환하며, 오류가 나면 nullptr을 반환합니다. 반환된 객체의 소유권은 호출자에게 넘어가며, 호출자가 이를 삭제할 책임을 가집니다. 요청은 완료 핸들러에서 삭제되거나, Request::reuse()로 상태를 초기화한 뒤 재사용될 수 있습니다. 호출자는 Request::addBuffer로 한 요청에 같은 스트림의 버퍼를 둘 이상 연결해서는 안 되며, 한 요청은 스트림당 버퍼를 하나만 포함할 수 있습니다.

Request::addBuffer()는 먼저 !stream 조건을 확인하고, 참이면 "Invalid stream reference" 오류 로그를 남긴 뒤 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. 다음으로 buffer->_d()->fence()가 남아 있으면 -EEXIST를 반환하므로, fence가 남아 있는 버퍼는 이 단계에서 등록되지 않습니다. 마지막으로 bufferMap_.try_emplace(stream, buffer)의 inserted가 false이면, 로그 "FrameBuffer already set for stream"과 함께 -EEXIST를 반환합니다.

!stream 검사, fence 검사, inserted 검사를 모두 통과하고 bufferMap_.try_emplace가 inserted가 true인 경우에만 buffer->_d()->setRequest(this)와 _d()->pending_.insert(buffer)가 이 순서대로 실행됩니다. 이 두 줄 뒤에는 fence 설정 분기가 이어지고, 함수는 return 0;으로 끝납니다. 애플리케이션은 createRequest()로 요청을 만든 뒤 queueRequest를 호출하기 전에 그 요청에 캡처 버퍼를 하나 이상 채워야 하며, 버퍼가 없는 요청은 큐에 넣지 않고 거부됩니다. Camera::queueRequest는 접근 검사에서 반환하지 않고 생성 카메라 검사에 도달한 경우, 요청을 생성한 카메라가 현재 카메라와 다르면 -EXDEV를 반환합니다.

Camera::queueRequest는 접근 검사와 요청을 생성한 카메라 검사를 통과해 상태 검사에 도달한 경우, request->status()가 Request::RequestPending과 일치하지 않으면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 접근, 요청을 생성한 카메라, 요청 상태 검사에서 반환하지 않고 controls 검사에 도달한 경우, request->controls().infoMap()이 Camera::controls()의 주소와 다르면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다.

Camera::queueRequest가 앞선 접근·요청 생성 카메라·요청 상태·controls 검사를 통과해 이 검사에 도달하면, buffers 목록이 비어 있는 경우 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. 앞선 검사에서는 접근 검사 결과가 음수이면 그 값을 반환하고, 요청을 만든 카메라가 다르면 -EXDEV를, 요청 상태나 controls 검사가 실패하면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. Camera::queueRequest가 앞선 검사와 빈 버퍼 검사를 통과해 스트림 순회에 도달한 경우, 요청의 각 스트림이 activeStreams_에 포함되어 있는지 검사하고 포함되지 않은 스트림이 있으면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다.

Camera::queueRequest()는 요청 검사를 마친 뒤 ConnectionTypeQueued를 지정해 invokeMethod로 PipelineHandler::queueRequest를 호출하고, 그 호출 뒤에 0을 반환합니다. 이 0은 invokeMethod 호출 뒤의 반환값이며, 요청 완료는 카메라가 requestCompleted 신호로 별도로 알립니다.
items.reason: 지역 그림들이 버퍼 연결의 거절 순서, 큐에 제출할 요청의 검사 조건, 반환과 완료 알림의 차이를 직접 설명합니다. 표시된 분기와 순서는 제공된 소스 발췌와 부합합니다.

items.title: 소유권과 재사용
items.question: 요청과 버퍼의 수명 및 펜스 소유권은 어떻게 관리되며, 버퍼를 재사용할 때 무엇을 해야 합니까?
paragraphs: Request::addBuffer는 버퍼에 대한 참조를 요청에 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 해당 버퍼가 유효하게 남아 있도록 보장해야 합니다. Request::addBuffer가 성공하면 유효한 Fence의 소유권은 buffer(FrameBuffer)로 이동합니다. 이때 fence는 buffer로 옮겨집니다.

addBuffer가 실패하면 fence의 소유권은 가져가지 않으며, 전달받은 fence는 변경되지 않고 그대로 유지됩니다. 펜스가 신호되지 않으면 요청은 타임아웃 후 실패합니다. 이때 버퍼에는 펜스가 그대로 남아 있으며, 애플리케이션은 다른 요청에 버퍼를 재사용하기 전에 FrameBuffer::releaseFence()로 이 펜스를 회수해야 합니다. Request::reuse는 flags에 ReuseBuffers가 설정된 경우 bufferMap_의 각 버퍼마다 buffer->_d()->setRequest(this)를 호출해 그 버퍼를 현재 요청에 연결한 뒤, _d()->pending_에 그 버퍼를 추가합니다.

Request::reuse()에서 flags & ReuseBuffers가 거짓이면 else 분기가 실행되며, 이때 bufferMap_.clear()를 호출해 bufferMap_의 모든 항목을 비웁니다. Request::reuse는 status_를 RequestPending으로 설정한 뒤, controls_와 _d()->metadata_를 각각 clear()합니다. Request::ReuseBuffers 플래그는 Request::reuse() 호출 시 addBuffer()로 이전에 추가한 버퍼를 다시 사용하여 기존 버퍼를 유지합니다. 다만 버퍼에 연결된 펜스는 재사용되지 않으며, 소스 주석은 펜스를 사용하는 경우 이 플래그를 피하도록 권고합니다.

items.body:
Request::addBuffer는 버퍼에 대한 참조를 요청에 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 해당 버퍼가 유효하게 남아 있도록 보장해야 합니다. Request::addBuffer가 성공하면 유효한 Fence의 소유권은 buffer(FrameBuffer)로 이동합니다. 이때 fence는 buffer로 옮겨집니다.

addBuffer가 실패하면 fence의 소유권은 가져가지 않으며, 전달받은 fence는 변경되지 않고 그대로 유지됩니다. 펜스가 신호되지 않으면 요청은 타임아웃 후 실패합니다. 이때 버퍼에는 펜스가 그대로 남아 있으며, 애플리케이션은 다른 요청에 버퍼를 재사용하기 전에 FrameBuffer::releaseFence()로 이 펜스를 회수해야 합니다. Request::reuse는 flags에 ReuseBuffers가 설정된 경우 bufferMap_의 각 버퍼마다 buffer->_d()->setRequest(this)를 호출해 그 버퍼를 현재 요청에 연결한 뒤, _d()->pending_에 그 버퍼를 추가합니다.

Request::reuse()에서 flags & ReuseBuffers가 거짓이면 else 분기가 실행되며, 이때 bufferMap_.clear()를 호출해 bufferMap_의 모든 항목을 비웁니다. Request::reuse는 status_를 RequestPending으로 설정한 뒤, controls_와 _d()->metadata_를 각각 clear()합니다. Request::ReuseBuffers 플래그는 Request::reuse() 호출 시 addBuffer()로 이전에 추가한 버퍼를 다시 사용하여 기존 버퍼를 유지합니다. 다만 버퍼에 연결된 펜스는 재사용되지 않으며, 소스 주석은 펜스를 사용하는 경우 이 플래그를 피하도록 권고합니다.
items.reason: 로컬 그림들이 요청과 버퍼의 수명, addBuffer의 성공·실패에 따른 펜스 소유권, 타임아웃 뒤 회수, 재사용 버퍼의 연결 순서와 펜스 재사용 권고를 직접 설명합니다. 제공된 소스는 그림의 관계를 뒷받침합니다. 타임아웃 그림의 FrameSuccess 캡션도 전체 상태 정의와 대조했습니다.

items.title: Responsibilities by class
items.question: Responsibilities by class
paragraphs: CameraManager is the entry point to libcamera, enumerating devices, associating them with pipeline managers, providing applications with access to cameras, owning camera objects, and managing their lifetimes in response to hot-plugging and hot-unplugging. Only one CameraManager instance may exist at a time, and creating an additional instance before deleting the existing instance results in undefined behavior.

Camera models a camera capable of producing one or more image streams from a single image source and is the main interface for configuring and controlling the device and capturing image streams. libcamera manages the lifetime of camera instances using std::shared_ptr, and instances must be created with create(), which returns a shared pointer. The constructors and destructor of Camera are private to prevent manual creation and destruction. Request is an object that allows an application to associate buffers and controls for each frame and queue them for processing by the camera device.
The cookie passed to the Request constructor is an opaque value for application use that is stored in the request and can be read at any time through cookie().

items.title: State and allowed calls
items.question: State and allowed calls
paragraphs: If the camera succeeds in acquire() while in the Available state, it enters the Acquired state.

Camera::configure() checks access from CameraAcquired through CameraConfigured and returns the result if it is negative; after setting the stream of each configuration to nullptr, the function returns -EINVAL if validate() is not CameraConfiguration::Valid. Then, if the return value of PipelineHandler::configure is nonzero, the function returns that value; on success, the function clears the active streams and checks cfg.stream() for each configuration. If a stream is null, there is code that prints a Fatal message using LOG, then clears the active streams and returns -EINVAL, but the Fatal log terminates the program immediately after printing the message. Once all streams have been processed, the function sets the state to Configured and returns 0.

If start() succeeds while the camera is in the Configured state, the camera enters the Running state. The camera enters the Stopping state when stop() is called while it is in the Running state. The camera returns to the Configured state when stopping is complete while it is in the Stopping state. release() leaves the state unchanged in the Available state and changes it to Available in the Acquired or Configured state.

The caller may call Camera::createRequest() only when the camera is in the Configured or Running state. Camera::queueRequest may be called by the caller only when the camera is in the Running state and returns -EACCES if the request cannot be queued because the camera is not running. Camera::start() may be called only when the camera is in the Configured state.
The Camera class generally does not synchronize functions that affect camera state with each other. The caller must ensure that these functions are synchronized when necessary.

items.title: Errors and termination
items.question: Errors and termination
paragraphs: Camera::queueRequest() returns 0 if it successfully queues a capture request and a negative error code if it fails; it returns -ENODEV if the camera is disconnected from the system, -EACCES if the camera is not running, and -ENOMEM if no buffer memory is available to handle the request; and if the result of isAccessAllowed(Private::CameraRunning), which checks the running state, is negative, it returns that value unchanged.

Camera::queueRequest() returns -EXDEV if the request was not created by this camera, and returns -EINVAL if the request's status is not Request::RequestPending or request->controls().infoMap() differs from &controls().

After allocating a request with createRequest(), the application must fill it with at least one capture buffer before queuing it. After checking the camera state, the owning camera, the request state, and the control information, Camera::queueRequest() checks for the presence of buffers and active streams and returns -EINVAL if there are no buffers or a buffer's stream is not active. Completion of a queued request is signaled through the requestCompleted signal.

Camera::stop() returns 0 in the actual implementation if the camera is not running; if the camera is running, it checks isAccessAllowed(Private::CameraRunning) and returns the result unchanged when it is negative. If the check passes, the function changes the state to CameraStopping, calls PipelineHandler::stop with ConnectionTypeBlocking, asserts that there are no pending requests, changes the state to CameraConfigured, and returns 0.

The API contract for Camera::stop() describes stopping capture and request processing immediately, canceling all pending requests, and completing them synchronously in an error state. The return value is 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise, with -ENODEV specified when the camera has been disconnected from the system.

items.body:
Camera::queueRequest() returns 0 if it successfully queues a capture request and a negative error code if it fails; it returns -ENODEV if the camera is disconnected from the system, -EACCES if the camera is not running, and -ENOMEM if no buffer memory is available to handle the request; and if the result of isAccessAllowed(Private::CameraRunning), which checks the running state, is negative, it returns that value unchanged.

Camera::queueRequest() returns -EXDEV if the request was not created by this camera, and returns -EINVAL if the request's status is not Request::RequestPending or request->controls().infoMap() differs from &controls().

After allocating a request with createRequest(), the application must fill it with at least one capture buffer before queuing it. After checking the camera state, the owning camera, the request state, and the control information, Camera::queueRequest() checks for the presence of buffers and active streams and returns -EINVAL if there are no buffers or a buffer's stream is not active. Completion of a queued request is signaled through the requestCompleted signal.

Camera::stop() returns 0 in the actual implementation if the camera is not running; if the camera is running, it checks isAccessAllowed(Private::CameraRunning) and returns the result unchanged when it is negative. If the check passes, the function changes the state to CameraStopping, calls PipelineHandler::stop with ConnectionTypeBlocking, asserts that there are no pending requests, changes the state to CameraConfigured, and returns 0.

The API contract for Camera::stop() describes stopping capture and request processing immediately, canceling all pending requests, and completing them synchronously in an error state. The return value is 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise, with -ENODEV specified when the camera has been disconnected from the system.

items.question: Which API calls have threadsafe and state conditions and caller synchronization obligations, and which completion functions must be called on the CameraManager thread?
paragraphs: Camera::createRequest() is a thread-safe function. Camera::queueRequest() is a thread-safe function. The caller must synchronize Camera::start and Camera::stop each with other functions that affect the camera state.

The pipeline handler must call completeBuffer() and completeRequest() on the CameraManager thread. The same rules as for completeRequest() apply to cancelRequest(), so it must be called on the CameraManager thread. Camera::requestComplete() calls requestCompleted.emit(request) to emit the requestCompleted signal in the path that reports request completion.

items.title: Disconnection and pending requests
items.question: How does disconnection affect state and access results, and what happens to notification and pending-request handling?
paragraphs: Camera::Private::disconnect() stores CameraConfigured only when the current state is CameraRunning, and skips this store in other states. Afterward, the function sets disconnected_ to true regardless of the state. According to the comment, the purpose of the state change is to allow the application to free resources and call release() before deleting the camera if the camera was running when the hardware was removed.

The two overloads of Camera::Private::isAccessAllowed return -ENODEV before checking the state if both !allowDisconnected and disconnected_ are true. The single-state overload returns 0 if the current state equals state, and the range overload returns the same value if the current state is at least low and at most high. If the state does not match, the overload first uses ASSERT to check whether state, or both low and high, are within the valid bounds of the state name array; on paths that pass this check, it logs an error and returns -EACCES. The error log prints () appended to from, and obtains the state names using currentState and state, or low and high.
Camera::disconnect() calls _d()->disconnect() and then calls disconnected.emit().

Execution check: The TODO in Camera::disconnect() leaves handling pending requests when the camera is disconnected while running as future work. The excerpted body calls _d()->disconnect() followed by disconnected.emit() and contains no code to cancel or complete individual requests.

items.body:
Camera::Private::disconnect() stores CameraConfigured only when the current state is CameraRunning, and skips this store in other states. Afterward, the function sets disconnected_ to true regardless of the state. According to the comment, the purpose of the state change is to allow the application to free resources and call release() before deleting the camera if the camera was running when the hardware was removed.

The two overloads of Camera::Private::isAccessAllowed return -ENODEV before checking the state if both !allowDisconnected and disconnected_ are true. The single-state overload returns 0 if the current state equals state, and the range overload returns the same value if the current state is at least low and at most high. If the state does not match, the overload first uses ASSERT to check whether state, or both low and high, are within the valid bounds of the state name array; on paths that pass this check, it logs an error and returns -EACCES. The error log prints () appended to from, and obtains the state names using currentState and state, or low and high.

Camera::disconnect() calls _d()->disconnect() and then calls disconnected.emit().

Execution check: The TODO in Camera::disconnect() leaves handling pending requests when the camera is disconnected while running as future work. The excerpted body calls _d()->disconnect() followed by disconnected.emit() and contains no code to cancel or complete individual requests.

items.title: Request creation and completion
items.question: Request creation and completion
paragraphs: createRequest returns a newly created empty Request object as std::unique_ptr<Request>, and returns nullptr if an error occurs. Ownership of the returned object passes to the caller, who is responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion handler, or reused after its state is reset with Request::reuse(). The caller must not add two or more buffers for the same stream to one request via Request::addBuffer, and a request can contain only one buffer per stream.

Request::addBuffer() first checks whether !stream is true. If it is, the error "Invalid stream reference" is logged, and -EINVAL is returned. Next, if buffer->_d()->fence() still exists, -EEXIST is returned, so a buffer that still has a fence is not registered at this stage. Finally, if inserted of bufferMap_.try_emplace(stream, buffer) is false, the log "FrameBuffer already set for stream" is written, and -EEXIST is returned.

buffer->_d()->setRequest(this) and _d()->pending_.insert(buffer) execute in that order only if the !stream check, fence check, and inserted check all pass and bufferMap_.try_emplace has inserted set to true. A fence-setting branch follows these two lines, and the function ends with return 0;. After creating a request with createRequest(), the application must fill that request with at least one capture buffer before calling queueRequest; requests with no buffers are rejected without being queued. If Camera::queueRequest reaches the check for the camera that created the request without returning during the access check, and the camera that created the request differs from the current camera, the function returns -EXDEV.

If Camera::queueRequest passes the access check and the check for the camera that created the request and reaches the status check, the function returns -EINVAL if request->status() does not match Request::RequestPending. If Camera::queueRequest() reaches the controls check without returning during the access, request-creating camera, or request status checks, the function returns -EINVAL if request->controls().infoMap() differs from the address of Camera::controls().

If Camera::queueRequest passes the preceding access, request-creating camera, request status, and controls checks and reaches this check, the function returns -EINVAL if the buffers list is empty. In the preceding checks, if the access check result is negative, the function returns that value; if the camera that created the request differs from the current camera, the function returns -EXDEV; and if the request status or controls check fails, the function returns -EINVAL. If Camera::queueRequest passes the preceding checks and the empty-buffer check and reaches the stream iteration, the function checks whether each stream in the request is included in activeStreams_ and returns -EINVAL if any stream is not included.

After completing the request checks, Camera::queueRequest() calls PipelineHandler::queueRequest through invokeMethod, specifying ConnectionTypeQueued, and returns 0 after that call. This 0 is the return value after the invokeMethod call; the camera separately signals request completion through the requestCompleted signal.

Next, if buffer->_d()->fence() still exists, -EEXIST is returned, so a buffer that still has a fence is not registered at this stage. Finally, if inserted of bufferMap_.try_emplace(stream, buffer) is false, the log "FrameBuffer already set for stream" is written, and -EEXIST is returned.

buffer->_d()->setRequest(this) and _d()->pending_.insert(buffer) execute in that order only if the !stream check, fence check, and inserted check all pass and bufferMap_.try_emplace has inserted set to true. A fence-setting branch follows these two lines, and the function ends with return 0;. After creating a request with createRequest(), the application must fill that request with at least one capture buffer before calling queueRequest; requests with no buffers are rejected without being queued. If Camera::queueRequest reaches the check for the camera that created the request without returning during the access check, and the camera that created the request differs from the current camera, the function returns -EXDEV.

If Camera::queueRequest passes the access check and the check for the camera that created the request and reaches the status check, the function returns -EINVAL if request->status() does not match Request::RequestPending. If Camera::queueRequest() reaches the controls check without returning during the access, request-creating camera, or request status checks, the function returns -EINVAL if request->controls().infoMap() differs from the address of Camera::controls().

If Camera::queueRequest passes the preceding access, request-creating camera, request status, and controls checks and reaches this check, the function returns -EINVAL if the buffers list is empty. In the preceding checks, if the access check result is negative, the function returns that value; if the camera that created the request differs from the current camera, the function returns -EXDEV; and if the request status or controls check fails, the function returns -EINVAL. If Camera::queueRequest passes the preceding checks and the empty-buffer check and reaches the stream iteration, the function checks whether each stream in the request is included in activeStreams_ and returns -EINVAL if any stream is not included.

After completing the request checks, Camera::queueRequest() calls PipelineHandler::queueRequest through invokeMethod, specifying ConnectionTypeQueued, and returns 0 after that call. This 0 is the return value after the invokeMethod call; the camera separately signals request completion through the requestCompleted signal.

items.title: Ownership and reuse
items.question: How are request and buffer lifetimes and fence ownership managed, and what is required when buffers are reused?
paragraphs: Request::addBuffer stores a reference to the buffer in the request. The caller must ensure that the buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is invoked. If Request::addBuffer succeeds, ownership of the valid Fence moves to buffer (FrameBuffer). At that point, fence is moved to buffer.

If addBuffer fails, ownership of fence is not taken, and the received fence remains unchanged. If the fence is not signalled, the request fails after a timeout. In this case, the fence remains in the buffer, and the application must retrieve this fence with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before reusing the buffer in another request. Request::reuse calls buffer->_d()->setRequest(this) for each buffer in bufferMap_ when ReuseBuffers is set in flags, to associate that buffer with the current request, and then adds that buffer to _d()->pending_.

In Request::reuse(), the else branch runs when flags & ReuseBuffers is false, and bufferMap_.clear() is called to clear all entries of bufferMap_. Request::reuse sets status_ to RequestPending, then calls clear() on each of controls_ and _d()->metadata_. When Request::reuse() is called, the Request::ReuseBuffers flag reuses the buffers previously added with addBuffer() and keeps the existing buffers. However, fences attached to buffers are not reused, and the source comment recommends avoiding this flag when fences are used.

items.title: Camera state and streams to check before allocation
items.question: Camera state and streams to check before allocation
paragraphs: Before calling allocate(), the camera must already have been configured with Camera::configure() and must be stopped, and the stream must belong to the active camera configuration. -EACCES is returned when the camera is not in a state where it can allocate buffers, and -EINVAL is returned when the stream does not belong to the camera or is not included in the active camera configuration.

items.title: Distinguishing duplicate allocation from export failure
items.question: Distinguishing duplicate allocation from export failure
paragraphs: If inserted from try_emplace is false, FrameBufferAllocator::allocate logs an error stating that the buffers have already been allocated and returns -EBUSY. FrameBufferAllocator::allocate() stores the return value of exportFrameBuffers() in ret and, if ret is negative, removes the corresponding buffers_ entry using buffers_.erase(it). When FrameBufferAllocator::allocate calls exportFrameBuffers, it returns the resulting ret regardless of whether the value is negative.

paragraphs: English translation · human review pending. Review states below refer to the Korean source.
Collects the meanings of abbreviations and domain terms that appear in the document.
Select an underlined term in the body text to see its meaning in place. You can also search for the term by name in document search.
Quick links: 0–9 · A · B · C · D · E · F · G · H · I · L · M · N · O · P · Q · R · S · T · U · V · W · ㄷ · ㅁ · ㅂ · ㅅ · ㅇ · ㅋ · ㅌ · ㅍ · ㅎ
3A: A collective term for auto exposure (AE/AGC), auto white balance (AWB), and auto focus (AF). These are representative algorithms that the IPA computes.
AF (Auto Focus): An algorithm that moves the lens position to bring the image into focus.
AGC (Automatic Gain Control): An automatic exposure algorithm that sets the exposure time and sensor gain to match scene brightness.
ASSERT: libcamera's debug-check macro. In debug builds, if the condition is false, it logs a fatal message and aborts execution.
AWB (Auto White Balance): An algorithm that estimates the color temperature of the illumination and sets per-channel R, G, and B gains so that white appears white.
bayer: A color filter array in which each pixel of the sensor records only one color among R, G, and B. Raw data in this format must go through demosaicing before each pixel has RGB values.
CCM: Means the IPU3 color correction matrix algorithm.
DEBUG: The name of the most verbose diagnostic level among log severity levels. Setting the log level environment variable to `DEBUG` yields detailed logs.
DMA (Direct Memory Access): DMA (Direct Memory Access) is a term for a method in which an I/O device reads from or writes to system memory directly.
DQBUF: DQBUF is an ioctl command that requests the next available buffer to be dequeued from a V4L2 device.
DRM (Direct Rendering Manager): A kernel subsystem that manages Linux graphics devices. DRM pixel formats identify the channel layout within a buffer.
DW100: A separate hardware device that corrects distortion by remapping the image according to a coordinate table. It is included in the NXP i.MX8MP and similar parts.
EBUSY: If FrameBufferAllocator::allocate() is called again for a stream that already has buffers allocated, it returns -EBUSY.
EEXIST: Returns the -EEXIST error when a buffer still has an unreleased fence or a buffer is already registered on the same stream.

EGL: An interface that connects the graphics API with the display, image, and buffer of the operating environment. This document covers the boundary where shared buffers are imported as graphics images.

errno: The standard error number that Linux functions use to report the cause of a failure. libcamera functions return this value as a negative number. For example, -ENODEV means no device, -EACCES means access denied, -EINVAL means invalid argument, -ENOMEM means out of memory, and -EXDEV means a resource that belongs to another object.
ETIMEDOUT: An error code indicating that the IPC response wait timer has expired. The timer setting value in this document is 2000ms.
FBO: Refers to a frame buffer object to which a texture is to be attached.

fence: A synchronization signal that indicates when a buffer may be used. If a valid fence is attached to a request, the request waits for this signal in the preparation stage. It is different from the request completion signal.
FPS: The number of frames per second.
GB: Means the green B shading coefficient in the lens shading correction table.
GCC (GNU Compiler Collection): A collection of GNU compilers that includes front ends for C, C++, and other languages.
GDB (GNU Project Debugger): A GNU debugger that stops a program under specified conditions and lets you examine its execution state after it stops.
GL: A prefix used in identifiers of OpenGL-family graphics APIs. In this document, GL formats indicate the channel composition of a texture.
GNU (GNU's Not Unix): GNU is an operating system composed of free software. The name is a recursive acronym meaning GNU's Not Unix.
GR: Means the green R shading coefficient in the lens shading correction table.

HAL (Hardware Abstraction Layer): A layer that lets the operating system handle hardware that differs by manufacturer through the same interface. The final deployment target of this project is the in-house Android Camera HAL.

IPA (Image Processing Algorithms): A separate module (.so) that contains image quality algorithms. It reads the statistics sent by the ISP and calculates the ISP settings to use for the next frame. It is separated from the libcamera core so that manufacturers can provide it without publishing its source.
IPC (Inter-Process Communication): A method by which separate processes exchange messages. Because an unsigned IPA module runs in a separate process, libcamera calls it through IPC.
IPU (Image Processing Unit): The name of Intel's family of image processing units. Generation numbers are attached to the name, as in IPU3 and IPU6.
IPU3 (Intel Image Processing Unit 3): A camera ISP included in some Intel laptop processors. libcamera has a Pipeline Handler and an IPA for this device.
IPU6: One generation of the Intel Image Processing Unit (IPU). The official documentation lists it as a supported target of the simple pipeline handler instead of a dedicated handler.

ISP (Image Signal Processor): A processing unit that converts raw (Bayer) data output by the sensor into an image that can be displayed on screen. It performs operations such as black level correction, lens shading correction, white balance, and debayering.
LOG: Uses the category and severity level specified by the caller.

LSC (Lens Shading Correction): Processing that corrects lens shading, the phenomenon in which the edges of an image are darker than the center or colors are distorted due to lens characteristics. It is applied by multiplying by a correction table that divides the image into a grid.
LUT (Look-Up Table): A method that precomputes calculation results into a table and retrieves them directly by input value. The LSC correction table falls into this category.
mali-c55: Arm Mali-C55 camera ISP. libcamera has a Pipeline Handler and an IPA for this device.
mojom: A file format that defines the functions and data types of the IPA interface. Proxy code is generated from this definition at build time.

NV12 (NV12): A 4:2:0 format that uses 8 bits per component. The first plane is luminance (Y). The second plane contains interleaved chroma data, in which Cb and Cr values are stored alternately, one each. The whole layout is placed in linearly contiguous memory.
OMM: An external documentation tool referenced by this site's reading-layout, figure zoom, and search rules. Only the rules were applied; the tool's runner was not used.

Pending: The request state in which the request has not yet changed to completed or canceled. It does not mean device processing has started, and if a preceding request is in this state, the return of a following request may also have to wait.

Pipeline Handler: A libcamera component that finds the media device of a specific hardware platform (IPU3, RKISP1, etc.), creates cameras, passes requests to the device, and returns their completion. There is one per platform.
PR (Pull Request): A request proposing that code changes be merged into the project.
QBUF: An ioctl that requests the addition of a buffer to the V4L2 device's queue.
RAW: RAW is a pixel color-encoding classification and is distinguished from StreamRole::Raw, a separate stream role for capturing raw sensor frames.
RK3399: Rockchip's system-on-chip (SoC). The official documentation lists it as a supported target of the rkisp1 pipeline handler.
RKISP1 (Rockchip Image Signal Processor 1): A camera ISP included in Rockchip SoCs, the NXP i.MX8MP, and others. libcamera has a Pipeline Handler and an IPA for this device.
ROI (Return on Investment): ROI is a concept that compares returns with investment costs, and it is not measured in this example from the public libcamera documentation.
STREAMOFF: An ioctl that requests streaming to be stopped for the specified buffer type on a V4L2 device.
TID (Linux thread ID): A TID is the Linux thread ID returned by the gettid system call.
UDMABUF (userspace dmabuf misc driver): A Linux kernel driver name for a driver that converts a userspace memfd region into a dma-buf.
UQ: An unsigned fixed-point format. UQ<m, n> represents a value with m bits for the integer part and n bits for the fractional part.
UVC (USB Video Class): The standard that USB webcams follow. libcamera handles this device with the uvcvideo Pipeline Handler.
V4L2 (Video4Linux2): The API through which the Linux kernel handles cameras and video devices. libcamera uses this API to control the sensor and ISP devices.

VM (Virtual Machine): A virtual machine is a computer implemented in software by virtualizing the resources of a physical computer, and it runs its own operating system and applications. It is not limited to cloud servers and can also be created on a personal physical computer.
WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux): A Windows feature that lets you run a Linux environment on a Windows computer.
WSL2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux 2): An environment for running Linux on Windows. This site is built from the results of building and extracting libcamera on WSL2.
Debayer: A process that interpolates the missing colors of each pixel from neighboring pixels in bayer raw data to create an RGB image. Also called demosaicing.

Metadata: Capture information checked alongside the image pixels. The metadata of a Request is provided as a ControlList, and the FrameMetadata of a FrameBuffer holds capture status, timestamp, bytes used, and so on. Whether the other fields of FrameMetadata are valid depends on the capture status.
Black level: The reference value the sensor outputs even when there is no light at all. The first stage of ISP processing subtracts this value.
Shader: A small program that runs on the GPU. A software ISP may perform debayering and color correction with GPU shaders.
Software ISP: A libcamera component that performs ISP processing on the CPU or GPU in place of a hardware ISP on devices without one. In the source, it is named software_isp or softisp.
Distortion correction: A process that straightens an image bent by the lens. The RKISP1 pipeline performs it by supplying a vertex map to the DW100 device.
Control information map: Information that indicates the control items and ranges to be used with the camera. The control list of a request must refer to that camera's information map.
Tuning file: A YAML file containing sensor- and platform-specific algorithm parameters (calibration tables, color matrices, etc.). IPA reads it when it starts.

Frame buffer: A FrameBuffer object that represents the memory region storing image data. It provides the file descriptor, offset, and length of each memory plane, along with per-frame metadata. The valid scope of the data and metadata differs depending on whether capture succeeds, fails, or is canceled.

Proxy: A proxy object that does not call the IPA module directly. It receives calls through the same interface and forwards them to an IPA thread or a separate process. It is automatically generated from mojom definitions at build time.
Active streams: A Stream connected to the current camera configuration. If a request buffer refers to a stream of a different configuration, the submission check rejects it.

items.title: Tuning file before calibration
items.question: Tuning file before calibration
paragraphs: RKISP1 and Mali-C55 each pass a file name formed by appending .yaml to the sensor model name, along with the fallback name uncalibrated.yaml, to IPAProxy::configurationFile(). IPAProxy::configurationFile() first searches for the requested name and returns the path if it finds one. It returns an empty string if it cannot find the requested name and the fallback name is empty; if a fallback name is provided, it searches for that name and logs a warning.

Both uncalibrated.yaml files list Agc, Awb, BlackLevelCorrection, and Ccm. The gamma entry is GammaOutCorrection for RKISP1 and Gamma for Mali-C55. The Mali-C55 algorithm build list includes gamma.cpp, an entry in the build list distinct from the Gamma entry in the YAML.

items.title: Texture format of the software ISP input buffer
items.question: How do the GL format and EGL image checks fail respectively, and when is the framebuffer attached?
paragraphs: createDMABufTexture2D() maps both GL_RED and GL_LUMINANCE to DRM_FORMAT_R8. GL_RG maps to DRM_FORMAT_GR88, and GL_RGBA maps to DRM_FORMAT_ARGB8888.

A format not handled by the switch in createDMABufTexture2D() goes to the default branch. This branch logs unhandled GL format at error level and returns -ENODEV. This branch contains no code that assigns a value to dmabuf_import_failed_.

createDMABufTexture2D() logs eglCreateImageKHR fail at debug level if the result of eglCreateImageKHR() is EGL_NO_IMAGE_KHR. It then assigns true to eglImage.dmabuf_import_failed_ and returns -ENODEV. createInputDMABufTexture2D() passes false as the last argument to createDMABufTexture2D(). createOutputDMABufTexture2D() passes true as the last argument.

createDMABufTexture2D() returns -ENODEV early if the GL format cannot be handled or EGL image creation fails. On a path that does not return through these error branches, if output is true, it calls attachTextureToFBO(eglImage) to attach the texture to a framebuffer object and assigns the return value to ret. If output is false, ret retains its initial value of 0, and the function returns ret at the end.

items.title: Lens shading correction in the software ISP shader
items.question: Under what condition do the two shaders correct lens shading, and what do they process before and after it?
paragraphs: In both shaders, main subtracts blacklevel from the constructed rgb and divides the result by 1.0 - blacklevel. If APPLY_LSC is defined, it then multiplies the RGB values read from lsc_tex by 4.0 and applies them to rgb. The packed shader uses textureOut as the texture coordinates, while the unpacked shader uses center.xy; 4.0 is the scale factor for converting UQ<2, 6> values to floating point.

The main function in both shaders then multiplies by the awb gains, clamps each channel between 0 and 1, and applies ccm color correction. It then clamps the values between 0 and 1 again, applies apply_contrast to each channel, and raises the values to the gamma power. The IPASoftIspInterface.init declaration takes fdStats and fdParams as arguments and includes lscEnabled among its return values. The declaration does not specify a connection between these items and the shaders' lsc_tex.

items.title: Module discovery and isolation conditions
items.question: Module discovery and isolation conditions
paragraphs: IPAManager::IPAManager first searches the user-specified ipa.module_paths, skipping empty paths and calling addDir() for each remaining path. If the list of specified paths is not empty but no IPAs are found, the constructor logs a warning. Next, if utils::libcameraBuildPath() is not an empty string, the constructor appends src/ipa to that path and calls addDir() with a maximum depth of 2. Finally, the constructor calls addDir() on the installed system path IPA_MODULE_DIR and logs a warning if no IPAs are found in the entire search.

IPAModule::match returns true if info_.pipelineVersion is greater than or equal to minVersion and less than or equal to maxVersion, and the result of strcmp comparing info_.name and name is 0; if any of these conditions is not met, the function returns false.

createIPA first searches for a module using module(name, minVersion, maxVersion) and returns nullptr if no module is found. If a module is found, the function creates a T::Threaded proxy when isSignatureValid(m) is true and a T::Isolated proxy when it is false. If isValid() on the created proxy is false, the function logs an error and returns nullptr; if it is true, the function returns the proxy.

IPAManager::isSignatureValid returns false if HAVE_IPA_PUBKEY is not enabled. If it is enabled, the function returns false if forceIsolation_ is true; otherwise, the function opens the IPA module file read-only. If the file cannot be opened or the file mapping result is empty, the function returns false. If both steps pass, the function passes the mapped data and IPA signature to pubKey_.verify, logs the verification result, and then returns that result.

items.title: Thread and process boundaries
items.question: Thread and process boundaries
paragraphs: The Threaded init template directly calls ipa_->init() with the supplied parameters. If the return type is not void, the template stores the call result in _ret and returns it; if the return type is void, the template returns no value. In the init branch, after calling the IPA method, the template passes the address of the thread object thread_ to proxy_.moveToThread.

The Threaded start template branch sets state_ to ProxyRunning, then calls thread_.start() to start the worker thread. It then uses proxy_.invokeMethod() to call ThreadProxy::start with the ConnectionTypeBlocking connection type and the generated parameters, and returns the call's return value. In the methods of {{proxy_name}}Threaded, the ordinary synchronous branch, excluding init, start, and stop, directly calls the method of the same name on ipa_ with the arguments it received and returns the call's return value.

The asynchronous method branch passes the check expression state_ == ProxyRunning to the ASSERT macro. If the check expression is false, ASSERT logs an error message at the Fatal level and aborts program execution. If NDEBUG is defined before including log.h, ASSERT generates no code. In the Threaded asynchronous branch, proxy_.invokeMethod uses ConnectionTypeQueued as the connection type when passing a ThreadProxy method.
The {{proxy_name}}Threaded constructor calls ipam->load(). If load() returns false, the constructor returns immediately.

The Threaded constructor calls createInterface() only if load() succeeds. If no pointer is returned, the constructor logs an error containing ipam->path() and returns. If a pointer is present, the constructor owns the interface through unique_ptr and passes the pointer to proxy_.setIPA(ipa_.get()). It then uses connect to connect each event to the corresponding Handler method of receiver this and sets valid_ to true.

The {{proxy_name}}Isolated constructor finds the worker path using resolvePath("{{module_name}}_ipa_proxy") and, if the path is empty, logs an error and returns. It then creates IPCPipeUnixSocket with ipam->path().c_str() and proxyWorkerPath.c_str() as arguments and, if isConnected() is false, logs an error and returns. If the connection succeeds, the constructor connects receiver this and callback &{{proxy_name}}Isolated::recvMessage to recv.connect, transfers ownership of ipc to ipc_ using std::move, and then stores true in valid_.

IPAProxy::resolvePath first examines execPaths_ in order, skipping empty directories, and returns the path if the path with file appended has execute permission. It then checks src/libcamera/proxy/worker in the build directory if utils::libcameraBuildPath() is not an empty string, or the installation directory IPA_PROXY_DIR if it is an empty string. If an executable path is found in the selected directory, the function returns that path; otherwise, the function returns an empty string.

readyRead logs an error and returns if an error occurs while receiving a payload from the socket. The function also logs an error and returns if the received data is shorter than IPCMessage::Header. It then looks for a waiting entry in callData_ using the message's cookie; if a matching entry exists, the function moves the payload into the response, sets done to true, and returns.

IPCPipeUnixSocket::sendAsync sends data.payload() via socket_->send and stores the return value in ret. If ret is nonzero, the function logs an error and returns ret; otherwise, the function returns 0.

items.body:
The Threaded init template directly calls ipa_->init() with the supplied parameters. If the return type is not void, the template stores the call result in _ret and returns it; if the return type is void, the template returns no value. In the init branch, after calling the IPA method, the template passes the address of the thread object thread_ to proxy_.moveToThread.

The Threaded start template branch sets state_ to ProxyRunning, then calls thread_.start() to start the worker thread. It then uses proxy_.invokeMethod() to call ThreadProxy::start with the ConnectionTypeBlocking connection type and the generated parameters, and returns the call's return value. In the methods of {{proxy_name}}Threaded, the ordinary synchronous branch, excluding init, start, and stop, directly calls the method of the same name on ipa_ with the arguments it received and returns the call's return value.

The asynchronous method branch passes the check expression state_ == ProxyRunning to the ASSERT macro. If the check expression is false, ASSERT logs an error message at the Fatal level and aborts program execution. If NDEBUG is defined before including log.h, ASSERT generates no code. In the Threaded asynchronous branch, proxy_.invokeMethod uses ConnectionTypeQueued as the connection type when passing a ThreadProxy method.

The {{proxy_name}}Threaded constructor calls ipam->load(). If load() returns false, the constructor returns immediately.

The Threaded constructor calls createInterface() only if load() succeeds. If no pointer is returned, the constructor logs an error containing ipam->path() and returns. If a pointer is present, the constructor owns the interface through unique_ptr and passes the pointer to proxy_.setIPA(ipa_.get()). It then uses connect to connect each event to the corresponding Handler method of receiver this and sets valid_ to true.

The {{proxy_name}}Isolated constructor finds the worker path using resolvePath("{{module_name}}_ipa_proxy") and, if the path is empty, logs an error and returns. It then creates IPCPipeUnixSocket with ipam->path().c_str() and proxyWorkerPath.c_str() as arguments and, if isConnected() is false, logs an error and returns. If the connection succeeds, the constructor connects receiver this and callback &{{proxy_name}}Isolated::recvMessage to recv.connect, transfers ownership of ipc to ipc_ using std::move, and then stores true in valid_.

IPAProxy::resolvePath first examines execPaths_ in order, skipping empty directories, and returns the path if the path with file appended has execute permission. It then checks src/libcamera/proxy/worker in the build directory if utils::libcameraBuildPath() is not an empty string, or the installation directory IPA_PROXY_DIR if it is an empty string. If an executable path is found in the selected directory, the function returns that path; otherwise, the function returns an empty string.

readyRead logs an error and returns if an error occurs while receiving a payload from the socket. The function also logs an error and returns if the received data is shorter than IPCMessage::Header. It then looks for a waiting entry in callData_ using the message's cookie; if a matching entry exists, the function moves the payload into the response, sets done to true, and returns.

IPCPipeUnixSocket::sendAsync sends data.payload() via socket_->send and stores the return value in ret. If ret is nonzero, the function logs an error and returns ret; otherwise, the function returns 0.

paragraphs: IPAIPU3Interface declares queueRequest(frame, controls), computeParams(frame, bufferId), and processStats(frame, frameTimestamp, bufferId, sensorControls) as [async] methods. IPAIPU3EventInterface declares paramsComputed(frame), metadataReady(frame, metadata), and setSensorControls(frame, sensorControls, lensControls).

IPARkISP1Interface declares queueRequest(frame, reqControls), computeParams(frame, bufferId), and processStats(frame, bufferId, sensorControls) as [async] methods. IPARkISP1EventInterface declares paramsComputed(frame, bytesused), metadataReady(frame, metadata), and setSensorControls(frame, sensorControls).

IPAIPU3EventInterface declares paramsComputed(frame), metadataReady(frame, metadata), and setSensorControls(frame, sensorControls, lensControls).

items.title: IPA object and shutdown order
items.question: IPA object and shutdown order
paragraphs: After successfully calling load() once on a valid module, the caller may call createInterface() as many times as the number of IPAInterface instances needed. The Threaded proxy's stop first asserts that the state is not ProxyStopping and returns if the state is not ProxyRunning. If the proxy is running, it changes the state to ProxyStopping, calls ThreadProxy::stop with ConnectionTypeBlocking, and then calls thread_.exit() and thread_.wait() in that order. It then dispatches this proxy's InvokeMessage on the current thread and changes the state to ProxyStopped.
If ipc_ is present, the Isolated proxy destructor creates a header with the Exit command and the value of seq_ before incrementing it, then sends the message via sendAsync().

items.body:
After successfully calling load() once on a valid module, the caller may call createInterface() as many times as the number of IPAInterface instances needed. The Threaded proxy's stop first asserts that the state is not ProxyStopping and returns if the state is not ProxyRunning. If the proxy is running, it changes the state to ProxyStopping, calls ThreadProxy::stop with ConnectionTypeBlocking, and then calls thread_.exit() and thread_.wait() in that order. It then dispatches this proxy's InvokeMessage on the current thread and changes the state to ProxyStopped.

If ipc_ is present, the Isolated proxy destructor creates a header with the Exit command and the value of seq_ before incrementing it, then sends the message via sendAsync().

paragraphs: IPAModule::load() returns false if valid_ is false and returns true if already loaded_. If dlopen then fails, the function logs an error and returns false. If it cannot find ipaCreate using dlsym, the function logs an error, closes the handle with dlclose, sets dlHandle_ to nullptr, and returns false. If it finds the symbol, the function stores the factory in ipaCreate_, sets loaded_ to true, and returns true.
IPAModule::createInterface() returns nullptr if the module is invalid or not loaded; if both conditions are satisfied, the function calls ipaCreate_() and returns its return value.

IPCPipeUnixSocket::sendSync calls call with the input payload, the response storage location, and the cookie from the input header, and checks the return value. If the return value is nonzero, the function logs an error and returns that value unchanged. On success, the function stores a IPCMessage constructed from the response in out if out is not null, and returns 0.

IPCPipeUnixSocket::call attempts to insert into callData_ using cookie as the key and response and false as the values. Without checking whether the insertion succeeded, the function uses the result's first field as iter to point to the entry. It passes message, not an iterator, to the socket's send; if the send fails, it uses erase to erase the entry pointed to by iter and returns the send's return value.

IPCPipeUnixSocket::call starts the timer at 2000ms and waits until the entry's done becomes true. While waiting, the function calls processEvents() on the current thread's event dispatcher if the timer is running. If the timer expires, the function erases the entry using erase and returns -ETIMEDOUT. If done becomes true and the call completes normally, the function erases the entry using erase and returns 0.

items.title: Initialization and crop settings
items.question: After calculating the grid using the sensor active area and the cell count limit, how is the result passed to the crop configuration?
paragraphs: Lsc::init() uses the width and height of the sensor's activeArea and calculates the cell size in each direction using ceiling division, based on a maximum of 73 horizontal cells and 56 vertical cells. It then uses std::bit_ceil to round each cell size up to a power of two and determines the number of cells by dividing the image dimensions by these cell sizes, rounding up. The logarithm of each block size is calculated by subtracting 1 from the std::bit_width of the corresponding cell size.

Lsc::init() stores whether the tuning data's type is polynomial. It then passes the tuning data, context.ctrlMap, channel keys r, gr, gb, and b, the calculated horizontal and vertical sample counts, and the sensor activeArea size to the common algorithm's lscAlgo_.init() and returns its return value.

Lsc::configure() stores the width and height of analogCrop and passes the horizontal and vertical cell counts respectively to calculatePositions(). calculatePositions() returns an array of positions obtained by dividing the index i by dimension - 1 in each dimension. Then Lsc::configure() passes the LSC active state, analogCrop, and the two position arrays to lscAlgo_.configure() and returns its return value.

items.title: Parameter update conditions
items.question: Parameter update conditions
paragraphs: Lsc::prepare returns when frameContext.lsc.update is false and frameContext.lsc.enabled is also false. When frameContext.lsc.update is false and frameContext.lsc.enabled is true, Lsc::prepare returns in two cases: first, if the absolute difference between frameContext.awb.colourTemperature and lastAppliedCt_ is less than kColourTemperatureQuantization / 2; second, if that difference is equal to or greater than the same threshold and quantizedCt equals lastAppliedQuantizedCt_.

Lsc::prepare records 1 in params->use.acc_shd if the earlier early returns are passed. This flag tells the kernel driver to read the LSC parameters passed from user space instead of the cached copy. Lsc::prepare assigns frameContext.lsc.enabled to config->general.shd_enable after passing the earlier early returns. Then, if frameContext.lsc.enabled is false, execution exits via return.

On the active path, Lsc::prepare sets the width and height of grid to numHCells_ and numVCells_, respectively. block_width_log2 and block_height_log2 are set to blockWidthLog2_ and blockHeightLog2_, respectively. grid_height_per_slice is set to IPU3_UAPI_SHD_MAX_CELLS_PER_SET divided by numHCells_.

When Lsc::prepare reaches the coordinate setup, if polynomial_ is true, 0 is assigned to each of grid.x_start and grid.y_start. If polynomial_ is false, (cropWidth_ - sensorWidth_) / 2 is assigned to grid.x_start and (cropHeight_ - sensorHeight_) / 2 is assigned to grid.y_start. On the active path, Lsc::prepare sets config->general.gain_factor to 0. When Lsc::prepare reaches that setting, the bl_r, bl_gr, bl_gb, and bl_b fields of black_level are all set to 0.

Lsc::prepare passes quantizedCt, which is frameContext.awb.colourTemperature quantized to kColourTemperatureQuantization, to interpolateComponents. Lsc::prepare assigns set.at("r")[i] to lut->sets[s].r_and_gr[c].r and set.at("gr")[i] to lut->sets[s].r_and_gr[c].gr from the LUT. set.at("gb")[i] is also assigned to lut->sets[s].gb_and_b[c].gb, and set.at("b")[i] to lut->sets[s].gb_and_b[c].b.
After filling the LUT, Lsc::prepare stores ct in lastAppliedCt_ and then quantizedCt in lastAppliedQuantizedCt_, in that order.

items.title: Once the allocator was prepared, the official cam capture finished.
items.question: Once the allocator was prepared, the official cam capture finished.
paragraphs: In this baseline reproduction, the default WSL kernel did not expose a DMA-BUF allocator, so the official cam could not allocate buffers.

The official cam, with source 293d751a left unmodified, was run separately in three independent processes on the WSL2 test kernel with the Virtual2 400x300 NV12 virtual camera configuration. In each run, normal completion of 3 frames and successful udmabuf allocation were observed, and the CPU access success of the separate DMA-BUF probe was recorded separately from this cam allocation observation. The trial ended with the default kernel restored, so in the current state this configuration cannot be rerun as is.

items.title: The virtual pipeline generates video and notifies request completion.
items.question: The virtual pipeline generates video and notifies request completion.
paragraphs: The virtual pipeline handler, analyzed from the pinned libcamera source, emulates a test virtual camera and supports software test patterns or image input as video in place of a real sensor. The Virtual2 configuration selected here is an example that supplies a 400x300 lines pattern, and this one configuration does not define the entire virtual feature. After allocation succeeds, cam attaches real DMA-BUF buffers to requests to prepare request delivery. This is the path in which the CPU attempts both NV12 conversion and writes to the mapped buffer together during software request processing.
The pattern generator attempts write-direction synchronization, and then attempts to map the buffer for writing within the scope of that synchronization.

Virtual requests are delivered asynchronously, and VirtualCameraData::processRequest waits until the target time before attempting pattern generation. Generation failures are marked with FrameError, which is the frame metadata state of the buffer, and receiving a buffer completion signal alone cannot establish that frame generation succeeded. completeBuffer returns a boolean indicating whether all buffers of the request have completed, and in the virtual pipeline's buffer completion path, completeRequest is called only when the returned boolean is true. A completed request whose turn in notification order has come is delivered to the cam callback connected to the requestCompleted signal, and if an earlier request is still incomplete, notification of later requests is held.

items.body:
The virtual pipeline handler, analyzed from the pinned libcamera source, emulates a test virtual camera and supports software test patterns or image input as video in place of a real sensor. The Virtual2 configuration selected here is an example that supplies a 400x300 lines pattern, and this one configuration does not define the entire virtual feature. After allocation succeeds, cam attaches real DMA-BUF buffers to requests to prepare request delivery. This is the path in which the CPU attempts both NV12 conversion and writes to the mapped buffer together during software request processing.

The pattern generator attempts write-direction synchronization, and then attempts to map the buffer for writing within the scope of that synchronization.

Virtual requests are delivered asynchronously, and VirtualCameraData::processRequest waits until the target time before attempting pattern generation. Generation failures are marked with FrameError, which is the frame metadata state of the buffer, and receiving a buffer completion signal alone cannot establish that frame generation succeeded. completeBuffer returns a boolean indicating whether all buffers of the request have completed, and in the virtual pipeline's buffer completion path, completeRequest is called only when the returned boolean is true. A completed request whose turn in notification order has come is delivered to the cam callback connected to the requestCompleted signal, and if an earlier request is still incomplete, notification of later requests is held.

items.title: Prepared initial requests are submitted within the limit.
items.question: How are prepared initial requests submitted within the limit, and how are queue returns handled?
paragraphs: After request preparation and camera start, cam submits only within the limit, omits the submission when the limit is reached, and the 0 returned in that case is not a success of the actual camera queue API. The actual camera queue API call checks the state and the request and may return an error; on success, the API call only schedules an asynchronous call and does not treat that as processing completion; if the initial submission fails, cam stops the camera that has already started.

items.question: How does cam process a completion notification in the event loop under the documented no-output-sink condition?
paragraphs: CameraSession::requestComplete returns without any processing if the request status is Request::RequestCancelled. For other requests, the call to CameraSession::processRequest is deferred to the event loop via EventLoop::instance()->callLater. The purpose is to avoid blocking the camera manager thread by handing processing of completed requests to the event loop, and the source comment states this purpose explicitly.

The three actual run commands this time did not request screen or file output options. Behavior that selects other output options was not verified by this run. When a processing limit is set and the processing count has already reached that limit on entry, processRequest returns immediately without issuing captureDone again, skipping subsequent frame processing.

processRequest outputs the frame information and increments the processed count by one. Afterward, when the processed count reaches the configured capture limit, processRequest emits the captureDone signal and returns from the function. Under the output condition defined earlier, CameraSession::processRequest reuses the request while keeping its buffers and calls queueRequest if the processing limit is unset or the processed count has not yet reached the limit. processRequest compares the processed count with the capture limit, and the submission attempt count is compared with the same capture limit in queueRequest, so the two checks differ in timing: one occurs when a request is processed and the other when it is submitted.

In this run, the request completion callback thread and the subsequent processRequest processing thread were different. However, this thread arrangement is not guaranteed in every run, and the RequestCancelled cancellation branch of requestComplete exists in the source but was not tested dynamically in this run.

items.title: Reproduction is performed after the supported kernel and device access are checked.
items.question: In the documented reproduction procedure, in what preparation order do the current environment assessment, separate approval for necessary shared host changes, booting a supported kernel and verifying device access, and running the official cam reproduction follow?
paragraphs: Preparation (1–3) Investigate the Kconfig and dependency conditions of the kernel to be used without changing the host.
Select a DMA-BUF allocator that matches the investigation results. When reproducing under the same conditions as this record, udmabuf is required.

Check only for the modules actually required by the selected kernel and allocator, whether they are installed and whether the kernel version matches. The recorded udmabuf trial used a built-in driver and did not install a separate module.

Host changes (4–5): Obtain separate approval for the host change plan immediately before execution, including the change proposal, kernel image SHA-256, impact, exact backup path, and recovery procedure. Do not substitute PR merge or Pages deployment approval for this host change approval.
Install and boot the trial kernel according to the approved plan.
Pre-execution checks (6–11) Check whether the running kernel matches 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2-issue211, and if it differs, do not capture.
In the WSL root child context, check whether you have access permission to open /dev/udmabuf, and if not, do not start capture.
Cross-check the size 400x300 and pattern value lines of the Virtual2 YAML to be used as a single configuration combination.
Check that the value of the camera selection argument --camera in the cam command to be run is Virtual2.
Check whether the cam stream argument to be used requests role=video,width=400,height=300,pixelformat=NV12.
Directly check whether the arguments of the official cam command to be run include --capture=3 and specify a request for 3 frames.
Run and verify (12–13) Following the linked execution procedure, run the official cam, whose source is unmodified, as three independent processes.

Use the new run results as evidence and cross-check them against a single expected result combination: camera Virtual2, actually applied stream 400x300 NV12, normal 3 frames for each independent run, and exit code 0.

Execution check item: The virtual capture results apply only to the WSL2 Virtual2 NV12 simulation configuration. Physical DMA, cameras, product applications, and the in-house HAL are unverified, and GDB affects timing, so the callback return instruction and performance were not verified.

items.title: Why request acceptance and completion are separated
items.question: Why request acceptance and completion are separated
paragraphs: After allocating a request with createRequest(), the application must fill it with at least one capture buffer before calling queueRequest. Requests without buffers are invalid and are rejected without being queued. After the request has been queued, the camera notifies its completion through the requestCompleted signal.

Even if the pipeline handler calls completeBuffer to signal that the last buffer of a request has completed, the request is not automatically completed at that point. This gives the pipeline handler an opportunity to perform any operations that may still be needed, and the handler must explicitly complete the request with completeRequest(). Requests are returned to the application in submission order, and the pipeline handler may call completeRequest() on any completed request without ordering constraints.
